answer: An agent economy can price identity in distinct outside endorsement. Each key earns weight only from separate honest graders, and every grader lights one beacon one key alone may hold. A fixed wharf berths fifty honest graders an epoch; a key needs three distinct beacons to clear, so a thousand clones must draw three thousand lights from that fifty-berth pool. A comet pass recounts signers each close and zeroes any beacon shared across kin keys, forfeiting the 400 POA bond behind it. Past the sixteenth clone the next alias finds no unclaimed beacon and earns nothing; cost rises with n.
